terms.grammar: conjunction with the subjunctive; also with an adjective or participle alone
evidence: Mart. 13.81.1: quamvīs lāta gerat patella rhombum
Plin. NH 9.25: quamvīs occultus atque abditus
terms.comment: Latin has no preposition for “despite”: “despite the cold” becomes a clause, “though it is cold”, with quamvīs, quamquam or etsī, and tamen often marks the main clause. With an adjective alone, “however …”: quamvīs fertilis.

terms.grammar: conjunction with the indicative; tamen in the main clause
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.53.1: etsī nihil habeō quod ad tē scrībam, scrībō tamen

terms.grammar: adjective, first and second declension; with a noun or pronoun in the ablative absolute: mē invītō, despite me
evidence: Cic. Att. 14.13.6: fēcisset nihilō minus mē invītō
Publil. Sent. R 26: quidquid invītō auferās
terms.comment: “Despite my wishes”: mē invītō, or contrā meam voluntātem. “Despite that”, “all the same”: nihilōminus (see however).

phrases.latin: ego etsī nihil habeō quod ad tē scrībam, scrībō tamen quia tēcum loquī videor
phrases.english: even though I have nothing to write to you, I write all the same, because I feel I am talking with you

phrases.latin: quamvīs lāta gerat patella rhombum, rhombus lātior est tamen patellā
phrases.english: however wide the dish that holds the turbot, the turbot is wider than the dish

phrases.latin: quamvīs sint sub aquā, sub aquā maledīcere temptant
phrases.english: though they are under water, under water they still try to curse

phrases.latin: ut ager quamvīs fertilis sine cultūrā frūctuōsus esse nōn potest, sīc sine doctrīnā animus
phrases.english: as a field, however fertile, cannot bear fruit without tilling, so neither can a mind without teaching

phrases.latin: etenim ille, quoniam semel indūxit animum sibi licēre quod vellet, fēcisset nihilō minus mē invītō
phrases.english: for once he had made up his mind that he could do as he liked, he would have done it all the same, despite me

phrases.latin: Rapere est, nōn petere, quidquid invītō auferās.
phrases.english: Whatever you take from someone against his will is grabbing, not asking.

phrases.latin: adjūrāsque id tē mē invītō nōn esse factūrum
phrases.english: and you swore you would not do it without my consent
